Regular meetings are held on the 4th Monday of every month at 8:00 a.m.

  CORONAVIRUS DISEASE (COVID-19) ADVISORY

following the State and County Health Department’s current Health Officer
recommendations to prevent and reduce transmission of COVID-19 by holding meetings
via teleconference.

  before or during the meeting, prior to the close of public comment on an item, to
  be read by the Board Chair during public comment. Lengthy public comment may
  be summarized in the interest of time.

BOARD OF TRUSTEES REPORTS

1. CHAIRPERSON REPORT

Chairperson Domier thanked everyone for their time, service, and effort put into the City and
thanked Staff for working with the Board to make the Library a focal point of the City. He shared
his hope to meet in-person for the next Board meeting. Director Johnson shared that she will discuss
this with City Manager Marlowe.

Chairperson Domier highlighted that the agenda format has changed per guidance from City Clerk
Baker. Management Analyst Shigenaga explained that City Clerk Baker has been working to make
agendas for the City’s boards and commissions uniform, with the main changes being Approval of
Minutes now falls under New Business and the removal of one Public Comments section. Trustee
Mollno expressed that Approval of Minutes should not fall under New Business, but instead Old
Business and requested the change be reversed. Director Johnson responded that staff will talk to
City Clerk Baker to discuss this. Chairperson Domier noted that everyone should have received an
email from City Clerk Baker regarding the public service ethics education, which should be
completed by the end of the month.

Chairperson Domier discussed the Board recruitment. He recalled that the Board sent an email to
the City Council on February 28 regarding the full staffing of the Board to include alternates. He
expressed his dismay that at the City Council meeting on March 9, Council voted to remove the

  4 of 22
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
APRIL 11, 2022  PAGE 2 OF 8

alternate positions. Director Johnson shared that on April 13, there will be a second reading of the
ordinance that modifies the framework of the boards and commissions. Council Member Ude
recalled that it was difficult to find members for all the boards and commissions, and requesting
people to serve as alternates with no official vote was an imposition on people’s time. Trustee
Mollno expressed her dismay to not have alternates. She shared that there have been instances in
the past where members weren’t fully committed to the Board and the alternates became very
important. In addition, she explained how in the past, applications have been submitted to join the
Board, but they were never considered. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth commented that she
doesn’t believe that the recruitment effort has been very strong in the past. In addition, she explained
that alternates are often viewed as members in training, as there is a lot to learn. She asked
Chairperson Domier if he could write an email to City Council on behalf of the Board re-iterating
their concern regarding the alternates. Chairperson Domier shared that he plans to attend the
meeting in person and speak on behalf of the Board. He added that when he first joined the Board,
he served as an alternate and agreed that it did serve as valuable training to learn the ropes. Trustee
Mollno added that alternates serve an important role in assisting the Board meeting quorum when
others are out.

Chairperson Domier commented that one of his goals is to forge closer ties with the other Library
support groups, the Friends and the Foundation. He shared how glad he is to have set up the liaison
roles to both of these support groups.

2. TRUSTEE REPORTS

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth shared that she was pleased and sad to see the article about a
Library Staff retiree on the front page of the newspaper. For the next Board meeting, she requested
to see the Donations Monitor, a spending plan for the Chinese Club donation carried over from FY
2020-2021, and an update on what is currently going on in regards to planning for the Summer
Reading Club. She also asked what the plans are for the next Board meeting. Chairperson Domier
responded that the plan is to see how this meeting goes in order to determine if the Board needs
to meet again in two weeks.

Trustee Chien, Trustee Mollno, and Trustee Derry did not have anything to report at this time.

3. CRAIN ART GALLERY LIAISON REPORT

Trustee Mollno shared how nice it was to finally have a meeting in person. She explained that last
month’s update on the exhibits has not changed. The current exhibit, the Verdugo Hills Art
Association, has been well received; following this exhibit will be April Drew Foster’s, which will be
up April 23 through early June. She explained that artists support the gallery by voluntarily donating
20% of any sales. The exhibits for Marian Fortunati and Marie McDuffie both did very well, resulting
in $370 and $1,600 donations respectively. She explained that the Committee would like to purchase
additional signage to inform people of the Art Gallery. In addition, the Committee doesn’t believe
that the Library’s main advertising should be through social media, but through other means as well
to reach those who don’t use social media. Finally, she noted that starting in June, Chairperson

  5 of 22
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
APRIL 11, 2022  PAGE 3 OF 8

Domier will need to appoint someone new to be the Crain Art Gallery Liaison. She did highlight
that she will be filling a vacant position on the Committee.

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth pointed out that regarding publicity, there was a section in the
packet that explained that a request for an additional staff member to manage the Department’s
publicity was denied. She asked what types of publicity would reach those who don’t use social
media. Trustee Mollno thinks that the San Marino Tribune and Pasadena Star News would be good
places to advertise the Library’s offerings. Director Johnson explained that she understands that
timely communication needs to be given to all audiences. She highlighted that the Department
doesn’t only use social media, but also sends out a monthly email blast, mails printed copies of the
Community Services Guide to each home, and has information on the Department’s webpages. She
explained that a recurring section in the Tribune will most likely prove to be too costly, but will talk
to the Tribune. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth shared that this was done in the past and it listed
upcoming events with limited details. Trustee Mollno added that not everyone is getting the weekly
or monthly e-blasts. She asked if the City could do a campaign to get the community on those mailing
lists. Director Johnson responded that she will pass this onto the City Manager’s Office, as this is a
priority of the Mayor.

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked if City Librarian Vera received an answer regarding serving
food at receptions. City Librarian Vera explained that the Department of Public Health’s guidelines
don’t really apply to the Library, as the Library isn’t a food service venue. She suggested that the
Library offer individually packed items.

Chairperson Domier thanked Trustee Mollno for her efforts as a liaison to the Crain Art Gallery.
He added that the Gallery is an incredible asset to the community and the Library.

Director Johnson asked Trustee Mollno who would be a good contact to request information for
an advertisement of the Crain Art Gallery to be published in the Community Services Guide. Trustee
Mollno shared that Lynda Lyons is the best contact. Director Johnson apologized for not thinking
to include the Crain Art Gallery earlier.

Trustee Mollno gave her Friends of the Crowell Public Library Liaison Report at this time. She shared
that a major concern that the Friends had was that they were not included in the last Community
Services Guide. Director Johnson clarified that the Friends were offered an advertisement back in
December, but they declined at the time.

Trustee Mollno shared that there was confusion regarding a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU)
between the Friends and the City; the procedure regarding the request of a donation had not been
followed in the past. She noted that the Friends are now accepting donations.

  6 of 22

4. SAN MARINO CENTER RENOVATION UPDATE REPORT

Chairperson Domier reported that he attended a virtual meeting on March 10 to discuss the
redesign of the San Marino Center, as a result of the environmental impact report (EIR). The findings
of the EIR do not set restrictions on the design of the rear of the building, so the architect is working
to make the rear of the building complement the Library. Another member of the Task Force noted
that shade is needed over the patio.

Council Member Ude added that he believes that the final quotes from the prescreened contractors
are being developed right now. He shared that the budget request should come to Council in June.

5. FRIENDS OF THE CROWELL PUBLIC LIBRARY LIAISON REPORT
Trustee Mollno provided this report after her Crain Art Gallery Liaison Report.
6. SAN MARINO PUBLIC LIBRARY FOUNDATION LIAISON REPORT
Trustee Chien reported that she attended her first meeting last month and will be attending her
second meeting tonight. She shared that her first meeting went very well; they discussed the
continued commitment of the Chang Group to the bookmark contest, a donation to the Library to
frame a picture, and future events. Director Johnson added that the picture is a night shot of the
Library that will be put on display in the upstairs administration office at the Library. Trustee Chien
shared that the Foundation is looking forward to the next Delicious Destinations. Director Johnson
added that the Foundation is looking to schedule a fall fundraiser, similar to Delicious Destinations,
which will require the closure of the Library, as well as an Open House in January of 2023.

Trustee Mollno requested that Lynda Lyons be made aware of the date of the fall fundraiser to make
sure the artist wants their work on display. Director Johnson agreed to let her know.

NEW BUSINESS

7. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Trustee Mollno noted that she was impressed with the detail of the Minutes. Vice Chairperson
Hollingsworth noted a typo on page 9 and moved, seconded by Trustee Mollno, to approve the
minutes with the typo corrected of the Library Board of Trustees meeting of Monday, February 28,
2022.

Motion passed by the following vote:

  Derry, Trustee Chien

ABSENT:  None

8. DIRECTOR AND CITY LIBRARIAN REPORT

In the interest of time, Director Johnson did not go through the Director and City Librarian Report
section by section, but asked if the Board had any questions. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked
what other vacancies the Library has, besides the librarians. City Librarian Vera responded that the
recruitment for the part-time Adult Services Librarian will begin this week. As far as other support
positions, the Library has no vacancies and is staffed to meet current customer needs. Director
Johnson added that existing staff will pick up additional hours to cover the hours worked by recently
retired Circulation staff.

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked what planning is going on currently for Summer Reading
Club. City Librarian Vera explained that a structure has been developed for the prizes, supplies are
in the process of being ordered, and communication with the schools to schedule school visits and
other marketing has begun. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth noted that the deadline for the last e-
newsletter for the schools is the week of May 9, with the last day of school being May 25.

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked if Beanstack is being used for Summer Reading Club. City
Librarian Vera responded that it is going to be used, but staff will also be evaluating if the community
feels engaged with it. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth thanked City Librarian Vera for all her work
on the Summer Reading Club.

Chairperson Domier encouraged the Board to help spread the word about the recruitment for the
soon to be vacant positions.

9. FY 2022-23 PROPOSED BUDGET

Director Johnson noted that Finance Director Chung is on the call. She explained the presentation
the Board will be receiving today highlights the significant changes made to the Library’s proposed
budget.

Director Chung explained that the City’s budget process began in January and ends in May or June.
With the help of the two Finance Liaisons, Mayor Jakubowski and Council Member Ude, he has been
able to improve the budget process over the years. He explained that the City’s largest revenue
source is property tax, which is expected to grow by 6%, and the City’s expenditures remain under
control.

Director Johnson highlighted that the Library’s revenue budget is $254,000 in the General Fund and
$41,000 in the Donations Fund. On the General Fund side, revenues are anticipated to reach FY
2018-19, pre-pandemic levels due to strong passport demand and on the Donations Fund side,
revenues are anticipated to increase as staff projects that more donations will be coming in next
year.

On the personnel side, Director Johnson shared that the full-time FTE is decreasing as the Director,
Management Analyst, and Recreation Coordinator salary allocations have been moved to the newly

  8 of 22
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
APRIL 11, 2022  PAGE 6 OF 8

created Community Services Administration as part of housekeeping. She explained that the part-
time FTE is proposed to increase by 1.59 with a nominal fiscal impact. Lastly, she shared that a title
change is requested to be more in line with industry standards: City Librarian to Library Manager.

Director Johnson then reviewed the Services and Supplies budget of $365,000, which is decreasing
by $63,000 from current fiscal year. In Administration, the decrease is because expenses have been
transferred to Community Services Administration Division. In Adult Services, the book budget is
decreasing by $15,000 as that money is being transferred to Children’s Services to allow for more
equal spending on book related items. The Children’s Services budget is decreasing because staff are
proposing a balanced budget for the Donations Fund and General Fund backfill is not repeated.
Management Analyst Shigenaga clarified that if one looked at the Donation Monitor presented back
in February, they would notice that the Children’s Service’s revenue budget for the current fiscal
year is significantly lower than the expenditure budget by about $21,000.

Trustee Derry asked why the book budget is decreasing in Adult Services. Director Johnson shared
that staff believe there is an imbalance in spending among Children and Adult. City Librarian Vera
added that purchasing patterns need to be evaluated; certain materials are shipped automatically,
but some of those are not being utilized by the community like they used to. She also explained how
physical magazines are not necessary anymore, as we offer access to them digitally. She believes that
staff need to pay attention to our patrons and purchase more of what they want, like best seller
books. She also re-iterated that it isn’t a decrease, but rather a shift of resources. Trustee Mollno
and Director Johnson shared year over year budget numbers are anomalies due to the pandemic,
which makes storytelling difficult. Trustee Mollno asked for an example of a book that is
automatically sent over, but not necessary in demand by the patrons. City Librarian Vera provided
an example of a book, which is typically used by high schoolers and is freely available online. Trustee
Mollno expressed her support for materials not being sent things automatically.

Director Johnson explained that the Processing budget is increasing. Given the size of the Library,
it is not a good use of staff time to process books in-house. Lastly, the Circulation budget is not
changing, as it is personnel based.

Director Johnson reviewed the upcoming capital projects. On the capital equipment side, the Barth
Room A/V is scheduled for FY 2022-2023 and the security camera system is scheduled for FY 2023-
2024. On the capital construction side, the Barth Room lighting design and Computer Room
renovation are scheduled for FY 2022-2023 and the Barth Room lighting construction is scheduled
for FY 2023-2024. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth thanked staff for moving the Barth Room A/V
project up a year.

Lastly, Director Johnson shared the upcoming important dates related to the budget; April 22 & 29
are preliminary budget study sessions and May 27 is when the proposed operating budget and CIP
will go to Council. She highlighted that the Community Services Department budget will be
presented on April 29.

Chairperson Domier thanked Director Johnson for the opportunity for the Board to review and
provide feedback on the proposed budget. He thanked City Librarian Vera for her diligence in
reviewing the Library’s budget.

Trustee Derry had no additional questions. Trustee Chien shared that she was concerned about the
decrease in the book budget, but feels more at ease after hearing City Librarian Vera’s explanation
for the shift in resources. Trustee Mollno did not have any questions at the time. Vice Chairperson
Hollingsworth asked why $9,000 will be unexpended in Other Contract Services (#101-93-4150-
0000), not in the Donations line items. Management Analyst Shigenaga clarified that the information
that Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth is referencing is discussing the year-end financials; $7,000 is
set aside for Chinese translation services and $2,000 is for cataloging. Vice Chairperson
Hollingsworth requested staff research how the Chinese Club donations are carried forward, make
sure they are earmarked specifically for what the donor intended, and communicate what the
spending plan is.

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked what Other Contract Services (#281-91-4150-2575) will pay
for and who is the donor. Management Analyst Shigenaga explained that the donation is expected
to come from the Friends to pay for adult program vendors and contractors for lectures and take
& makes. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth requested that “- Friends” be added to the name of that
line item. Management Analyst Shigenaga noted that the Finance Department is in charge of the
naming convention of line items. Director Chung agreed to research this and make the change.

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked what Other Contract Services (#281-92-4150-2575) will pay
for. Management Analyst Shigenaga responded that this money is expected to pay for Summer
Reading Club, seasonal performances, and other program vendors/contractors. Vice Chairperson
Hollingsworth asked what contractors would do. Director Johnson responded that they would be
program specific contractors. She also shared with the Board that staff submitted a detailed letter
to the Friends, which laid out how the donation money would be spent. Vice Chairperson
Hollingsworth noted that the Friends are a 501(c)(3), so they can designate how they would like the
money to be spent. Management Analyst Shigenaga responded that if the Friends chose to designate
the money differently, staff would need to take a budget amendment to Council to adjust the budget.
Director Chung added that staff cannot make any changes to the budget without Council approval,
but budget amendments can be made throughout the year.

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked what Materials & Supplies (#281-92-4376-2575) will pay for.
City Librarian Vera responded that this money will pay for program supplies and any other hands
on opportunities.

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked where the Donations Fund reserve balances will show in the
budget draft that Director Chung will be presenting to Council. Director Chung replied that the
remaining fund balances are not presented during the budget study session; rather, those are
presented to Council in October when the books are closed.

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth noted that because the March meeting was cancelled, the Board
has not seen the latest quarterly budget report. Management Analyst Shigenaga responded that it is
scheduled to come to the Board next month.

Chairperson Domier proposed that the Board cancel the second April meeting. Trustee Mollno
noted that the California Education Code requires the Board meet once a month, so mindful planning
is required when scheduling meetings. Chairperson Domier asked how the Board will know in
advance of the May meeting if they can meet in person. Director Johnson shared that she will talk
to the City Manager and send out an email announcement to all.

SUBJECT:  DIRECTOR AND CITY LIBRARIAN REPORT

BACKGROUND

At the request of the Library Board of Trustees, the Community Services Director and City
Librarian / Library Manager provide a monthly report to the Crowell Public Library Board of
Trustees. The report provides relevant administrative, operational, and financial updates, as well
as information on upcoming events, marketing and communication efforts, and customer
feedback.

DISCUSSION

Personnel Updates
  • An offer and acceptance has been made for the Adult Services Librarian II position. The
  candidate’s start date will be Tuesday, July 5. We look forward to sending out an official
  announcement on or around that date.
  • Critically-low PT staffing levels are straining daily library operations. There are (6) PT
  vacancies for Library Assistants/Librarians, and (1) PT Library Assistant on indefinite
  medical leave. We anticipate this critically-low level of staffing to continue for the next
  12-14 weeks (end of August). Staff are working diligently to shift all available employee
  resources to minimize the impact on library service levels, in conjunction with aggressive
  recruitment, selection, and on-boarding of new employees.

FY 2021-22 Q3 Operating Budget Summary Reports
See Attachment 1 for the Budget Monitor and Attachment 2 for the Donations Monitor.
Comments can be found on the right-most column of each.

Capital Priority List
At the April meeting, the Board requested that the Capital Priority List be updated and brought
back for the Board’s review. It is included as Attachment 3.

  12 of 22
 Advisory Body Recruitment (Commissions, Boards, Committees)
As of this writing, the Department’s Council Liaisons Talt and Ude will be conducting
interviews with the (4) Library Board applicants (2 full members and 2 alternates) on Tuesday,
May 24. The aim is to bring the appointment recommendations to the City Council at the May
27 meeting.

Advisory Body Training
City Clerk Baker and City Attorney Montes will provide a 30-60 minute training at the June 27
Board meeting. Training topics will include Board Member’s role and responsibility, decorum,
the Ralph M. Brown Act, and how to conduct successful meetings.

San Marino Public Library Foundation (SMPLF) Update

  Foundation Board Members - At the May meeting, the Board voted to invite Shawn
  Chou to join the Board beginning July 2022. Mr. Chou is currently serving on the Board
  for the Chinese Club of San Marino after serving as President. In the upcoming
  June meeting, officers for the 2022-2023 term will be confirmed.

  Foundation Operations - The Foundation will be transitioning to QuickBooks to
  provide better reporting and endowment fund tracking. QuickBooks is also able to
  work with the donor tracking software.

  Literary Libations: A Fall Event - The event idea is being developed and event
  committees are being formed. The Board decided to engage Alexander's Catering to
  provide services for this event. Alexander's Catering provided
  outstanding food for Delicious Destinations. Advance research is showing event
  costs will potentially be 15-25% higher. Many ideas are abound relating to literary
  references and libations.

  Dumpling Party - The Dumpling Party hosted by Sylvia Koh and her friends was held
  May 12 at the Chinese Club of San Marino. The Foundation is very grateful to the
  Chinese Club for providing their kitchen for the event. The event was
  successful with over 35 people in attendance learning how to make Chinese dumplings.
  Attendees were treated to fresh cooked dumplings and then shown how to make them
  from start to finish.

Friends of Crowell Public Library (CPL) Update
The annual donation request letter ($30K) supporting the FY 2022-23 Library Division budget
was sent to the Friends of CPL Board in early March; City staff have yet to receive a response.
A second follow up email was sent on Thursday, May 19 requesting a reply.

  Toastmasters Talk of the Town
  San Marino’s Toastmasters group has resumed their on-site meetings. The six primarily
  returning participants were offered the opportunity to hone their presentation and
  speaking skills in a supportive and convenient setting.

  iPhone Beginner Class
  This class was made possible by the CDBG program and its popularity extended the
  classes into May by participant request. The 10 learners were taught by community
  favorite Samuel Edison, who provided guidance and support to seniors as they became
  comfortable with their iPhone features and apps.

  Huntington Nurses Health Screening
  Huntington Hospital’s Nurses’ outreach project continues at Crowell Library, with
  patrons being screened for hypertension, heart disease, and diabetes. A second nurse has
  come on board so our patrons can be more quickly screened.

  14 of 22
   Coffee, Tea, and Chat
  On April 29, 13 attendees were present at this Mandarin-language program. The theme
  for this session was “Failure to Launch.” Programs such as this support community
  engagement as well as personal growth and enrichment.

  Chinese Club
  On May 12, 8 participants learned how to make scented sachets, which are used during
  the Dragon Boat Festival. Activities like these provide opportunities to share and
  appreciate cultures while engaging in community-rooted social activities.

  Youth Programs
  Storytime
  Storytime families were treated to a wide variety of classic and popular themes, such as
  “spring,” “robots,” and “emotions.” Toddlers did their best robot impressions while
  reading “Beep! Beep! Go to Sleep!” by Todd Tarpley. All ages got to practice identifying
  body parts with the weekly silly song, “Sticky Sticky Bubblegum.” 123 children joined Staff
  at the 8 storytimes.

  AAPI Heritage Storytime
  In partnership with a local volunteer organization, children in kindergarten through 3rd
  grade participated in a celebration of AAPI Heritage Month. This event consisted of
  stories and crafts that honor Asian Heritage. 40 patrons attended.

  Earth Day STEAM Take & Make
  This month’s take & make activity focused on recycling and reusing materials to make fun
  STEAM projects. Participants made flowerpots out of recycled cans from home, and then
  made their own seed sprout greenhouses to plant in their new flowerpot. Our Earth Day
  scientists then headed outdoors to go on a nature scavenger hunt, and finished up by
  creating an “indoor rainstorm” experiment using water, shaving cream, and food coloring.
  35 children participated.

  YA DIY Eco-Friendly Canvas Bag
  Teens were also inspired by Earth Day and got to create eco-friendly canvas bags. Armed
  with fabric markers in a rainbow of colors and an Earth patch in the shape of a heart,
  teens showed their love for the Earth by wearing their heart on their sleeve! 5 teens
  participated.

  Passports
  Passport Services continue to be in high demand. In the month of April, 452 passports
  were processed, which resulted in revenue of $17,515.

Public Works / Facility Maintenance Updates
Pending projects -
  • Story Walk at Lacy Park – the completion of this project has been delayed due to staffing
  capacity issues within the Parks & Public Works Department. Estimated completion has
  been moved to June.

  The Summer Guide has been delivered to residents. The production for the Fall Guide

MINUTES
  MEETING OF THE SAN MARINO
  LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES
  MONDAY, MAY 23, 2022 AT 8:00 A.M.
  VIA TELECONFERENCE

CALL TO ORDER: Chairperson Domier called the meeting to order at 8:02 a.m. via
teleconference.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Chairperson Domier led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL:  PRESENT: Chairperson Domier, Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth, Trustee
  Mollno, Trustee Derry, and Trustee Chien

  ABSENT: None

  CITY STAFF PRESENT: Community Services Director Johnson, City
  Librarian Vera, and Management Analyst Shigenaga

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

BOARD OF TRUSTEES REPORTS

1. CHAIRPERSON REPORT

Chairperson Domier shared his disappointment that the Board could not meet in person to say
goodbye to Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth and Trustee Mollno, but mentioned that there will be
a special City Council meeting in June or July to acknowledge all former members. He thanked both
for their service, passion, dedication, and guidance over the last few years.

Chairperson Domier highlighted that the Advisory Body Training has been moved to next month to
allow the new members to be included. He added that interviews for the potential new members
are scheduled for tomorrow.

2. TRUSTEE REPORTS

Trustee Derry and Trustee Chien did not have anything to report at this time.

Trustee Mollno thanked Chairperson Domier for his kind words. She shared how she reflected on
her experience of getting recruited to serve on this Board, knowing that today’s meeting is her last.
She commented that she intends to keep the Library very close, as she will stay on the Crain Art
Gallery Committee and might get involved in the Friends’ Book Shoppe. She thanked Vice
Chairperson Hollingsworth for her years of service on the Board.
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
MAY 23, 2022  PAGE 2 OF 6

Trustee Chien commended Trustee Mollno for being so knowledgeable on the rules and regulations
of the Board. She expressed her concern for losing that knowledge. Trustee Mollno shared that she
will try to provide suggestions when available. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth commented that she
believes the Library has knowledgeable staff who can assist with any questions that may come up.
She also added that some of the legal stuff is explained in the binder that members are given when
appointed. She explained that it has been a privilege to serve on the Board and hopes that the Board
will continue to support the staff and monitor the budget.

3. CRAIN ART GALLERY LIAISON REPORT

Trustee Mollno shared that April Drew Foster’s exhibit is on display right now and that her
reception went very well. She recommended that the Board attend the artist receptions to
represent the Library and show their support. She shared that the Committee is still looking into
some kind of signage that can make people aware of receptions and that artwork on display is
available for purchase. She added that staff will be purchasing lightbulbs and may be looking to
purchase an additional floor easel or two for the Gallery. She noted how pleased she was with the
marketing and publicity for April Drew Foster’s exhibit and reception.

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth highlighted the donations reported on the Donation Monitor from
the Crain Art Gallery. Trustee Mollno noted that a majority of the donations came from artist Marie
McDuffie and that donations are significantly higher when in-person receptions occur.

Director Johnson commended City Librarian Vera and Management Analyst Shigenaga for the
marketing of Library programs through the City Manager’s Weekly Briefing, social media, and the
Community Services Guide. She pointed out that there is a standing advertisement for the Crain
Art Gallery on the back cover of the Guide. Trustee Mollno pointed out that despite “liking” the
Library on Facebook, the Library’s content never shows up on her feed, so she recommended that
staff not rely heavily upon Facebook.

Chairperson Domier noted that Trustee Mollno’s comment about the Board attending artist
receptions is important to keep in mind and that he will try to attend them in the future.

4. SAN MARINO CENTER RENOVATION UPDATE REPORT

Chairperson Domier reported that he attended a meeting two weeks ago where the final plans were
reviewed. He shared that minor tweaks were made in hopes of making the building complement the
Library and that everything will be presented to City Council on June 8 at 6 PM. He encouraged all
to attend, as this project is not guaranteed to move forward.

5. FRIENDS OF THE CROWELL PUBLIC LIBRARY LIAISON REPORT
Trustee Mollno reported that she attended a meeting, but was unable to obtain the minutes. She
also pointed out that Chairperson Domier will need to find a new Member to serve as the Liaison
to the Friends moving forward.
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
MAY 23, 2022  PAGE 3 OF 6

Chairperson Domier pointed out an inaccurate statement in the mailer that the Friends sent out.
The statement read that the Friends solely funded the new self-check out kiosks installed in the
Library last year. Chairperson Domier clarified that the Foundation funded that project. Trustee
Mollno agreed to pass this information onto the Friends. Director Johnson pointed out another
potential false statement and shared that it would be appreciated if comments about a budget gets
verified with those that manage it. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth noted the importance of better
communication and working relationships between the support groups. Chairperson Domier shared
his hope to increase the Friends membership in the future, but doesn’t want to upset any support
group.

6. SAN MARINO PUBLIC LIBRARY FOUNDATION LIAISON REPORT
Trustee Chien reported that she attended two meetings. She shared that the fall fundraiser,
tentatively scheduled on October 15, may be called Literary Libations; pricing is still being discussed.
She noted how excited the Foundation is that Director Johnson is so willing to assist, especially with
marketing. Director Johnson highlighted that she manages the content of the Community Services
Guide and shared that the fundraiser can be showcased on the front cover, with more space on the
inside of the book.

Trustee Chien also reported that the Dumpling Party occurred, but she has not heard the details of
how it went. She also shared that a new officer has been added; his name is Shawn Chou.

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth requested that Trustee Chien let the Foundation know that she
recommends to advertise a project when marketing the fundraiser. Director Johnson shared that
discussions have occurred to decide on a large-scale project. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth added
that before the project gets decided, the Board needs to approve it. Director Johnson responded
that the Board will get to review the project in July or August. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth
noted the importance of the Capital Priority List, as it would have priority projects decided by the
Library to share with donors. Trustee Chien asked if it should be one major project, or a list of
projects. Chairperson Domier responded that it should focus on one project to be most effective.
Director Johnson added that she will work with the Foundation and City Administration on this.

NEW BUSINESS

7. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth moved, seconded by Trustee Mollno, to approve the minutes of
the Library Board of Trustees meeting of Monday, April 11, 2022.

Motion passed by the following vote:

AYES:  Chairperson Domier, Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth, Trustee Mollno, Trustee
  Derry, Trustee Chien
NOES:  None

MAY 23, 2022  PAGE 4 OF 6

ABSTAIN:  None
ABSENT:  None

8. DIRECTOR AND CITY LIBRARIAN REPORT

Director Johnson thanked Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth and Trustee Mollno for their time and
work on the Board. She shared how important their knowledge and guidance has been. She also
added that the City Clerk and City Attorney guide and train all Boards and Commissions to ensure
that all are knowledgeable of responsibilities, decorum, Brown Act, positional authority, etc.

She shared how thrilled she is to have offered the Adult Services Librarian II position to someone,
who is scheduled to start in early July. On the other hand, she shared that part-time staffing levels
are critically low, for various reasons; if staffing levels drop any lower, operating hours may be
modified. Trustee Mollno asked if the vacant positions can be filled by those without library training
and Director Johnson and City Librarian Vera explained that ideally, candidates have a library
background and working knowledge of libraries and everything they entail. Director Johnson shared
that there is a game plan in place to fill the positions as soon as possible. Trustee Mollno asked if
volunteers can be recruited to assist and Director Johnson responded that people can apply to be
City staff, but it cannot be on a volunteer basis. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth added that if staff
need assistance making a staffing request to the City Manager and City Council, the Board can
support. Director Johnson responded that such a request will most likely be made next year in the
budget process. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth also explained that a few years ago they considered
closing the Library on Sundays, but realized it would not save much money. She asked if staff had
considered closing on Sundays in June and July. Director Johnson responded that staff have
considered it, but was recommended by City Manager Marlowe to consider other options. Vice
Chairperson Hollingsworth asked if Sundays are the least used days. City Librarian Vera responded
that Sundays are a busy day; weekdays from 8-9 PM is when headcount is lowest. Vice Chairperson
Hollingsworth agreed that analysis of the hourly headcounts will be beneficial, but wants to suggest
more of a short-term solution. Trustee Mollno agreed with Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth.
Director Johnson clarified that temporarily closing on Sunday would actually be through August as
that is when hiring is expected to be done. Chairperson Domier expressed his confidence in
Director Johnson and City Librarian Vera in finding a solution that will please all. Vice Chairperson
Hollingsworth encouraged staff to launch Storywalk in late September or early October. Director
Johnson shared that the other reason why it is postponed is because of Public Works vacancies.
Trustee Mollno asked for an update on Summer Reading Club. Director Johnson responded at City
Librarian Vera will respond to that later.

Director Johnson moved onto the financial reports. She explained that Attachment 1 shows the
operating budget expenses through the end of March. Chairperson Domier asked what the
CENIC rebate is. City Librarian Vera responded that CENIC is how the Library receives high
speed broadband Internet at a discounted rate. Director Johnson explained that passports are off
the charts, helping the Library reach the revenue budget for the year. She added that other
expenses are well underbudget, but this is reflective of the current staffing levels. Vice Chairperson
Hollingsworth asked what repair was done to the Barth Room A/V and how much it cost.
Management Analyst Shigenaga responded that it cost $1,600 and that she will need to ask for a
copy of the invoice to figure out what exactly it was for. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth noted
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
MAY 23, 2022  PAGE 5 OF 6

that the Barth Room A/V will be remodeled as part of a CIP project and does not want the Library
wasting money to repair the current system when it will be completely replaced. Management
Analyst Shigenaga responded that a vendor did come out to check out the equipment a month or
two ago, but staff decided not to move forward for that very reason. Vice Chairperson
Hollingsworth asked why staff do not plan to spend the balance for the two book line items by
year end. City Librarian Vera responded that the Library needs staff in order to purchase books;
current full-time staff are doing everything they can to order books. Trustee Mollno asked why the
donation reserve fund balance has not increased despite receiving donations in the current fiscal
year. Management Analyst Shigenaga responded that the balance only gets updated once a year
after the books are closed for the fiscal year. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth explained to the
Board that unspent revenue should hit the reserve fund balance after the close of the fiscal year
and shared her hope to spend donations.

Director Johnson moved onto the Capital Priority list, which includes upcoming pending projects
and completed projects. She added that the Board will be hearing about the project that the
Foundation will be fundraising for, which is a one desk model. City Librarian Vera explained that a
one desk model means that there is a single service point, which will increase teamwork and
communication among staff. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked if that will do away with the
physical location of the existing reference desk. City Librarian Vera responded that there are plans
for what to do with the desk, as staff will no longer be working there. Vice Chairperson
Hollingsworth shared other libraries in the area that use this model and that the original designer
of the building has mentioned it as well. She also thanked staff for moving the Barth Room A/V
project up a year and Chairperson Domier thanked staff for putting together this document. Vice
Chairperson Hollingsworth pointed out that this list includes big ticket items regardless of who
the Library asks to pay, so the remodel of the circulation area would go on here.

Director Johnson shared that she hopes to welcome new members to the Board. She shared that
she will be serving on the interview panel tomorrow. She explained how the next section of her
report includes updates from the Library’s partners; however, staff have been unsuccessful in
receiving an update from the Friends. Director Johnson then highlighted some of the upcoming
events that the Department has scheduled.

Trustee Mollno asked for more information on the Summer Reading Club. City Librarian Vera
responded that the flyer does advertise that there are activities for both children and adults. She
explained that the reason why the link was not provided in the Guide was that they did not want
patrons going to a website that is not live. She added that details will be included in the Weekly
Briefing and other forms of communication, and outreach to the schools is occurring.

Chairperson Domier thanked staff and the Board for their time and dedication.
